subject.title: Add accessibility config option to disable emojis and unicode symbols in TUI

question: Should OpenClaw add a durable core TUI plain-text accessibility setting, and what public config key, default, and ASCII replacement semantics should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but naming and behavior for a new public config surface become compatibility and UX contracts for every TUI user.

options.title: Add Bounded TUI Plain-Text Mode
options.body: Implement an opt-in setting with ASCII replacements across tool cards, selectors, generated config metadata, docs, and tests while retaining rich glyph output by default.

options.title: Defer Until Semantics Are Chosen
options.body: Keep the issue open but pause implementation until maintainers choose the key, default, and replacement strings.

options.title: Reject Core Config For Now
options.body: Close only if maintainers decide glyph suppression should not be a core TUI capability despite the screen-reader reports.

recommendation.title: Add Bounded TUI Plain-Text Mode
recommendation.body: Implement an opt-in setting with ASCII replacements across tool cards, selectors, generated config metadata, docs, and tests while retaining rich glyph output by default.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest routing signal is original and recent TUI/tool-display/config ownership across the affected files.
